zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Takwīr
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾: the meaning of ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾ is: its light was gathered together and wound up, as the turban is wound. One says «كُرْتُ العِمامَةَ عَلى رَأْسِي، أكُورُها» and «كَوَّرْتُها أُكَوِّرُها» when I wind it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ﴾: «اِنْكَدَرَتْ» means they fell one after another and were scattered.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا الجِبالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾: they became a mirage.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا العِشارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾: «اَلْعِشارُ» are the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies; the singular is «عُشَراءُ». They are called «عِشارٌ» only because when ten months have passed over her — and she gives birth, when she gives birth at full term, in a year — she is an عُشَراء, the finest she can be in pregnancy; and her owners do not neglect her except in the situation of the Resurrection. The Arabs were addressed with the matter of the ʿishār because their wealth and livelihood were mostly from camels.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿وَإذا الوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾: it was said: "The wild beasts will all be gathered, even the flies; they will be gathered for retaliation."
﴿وَإذا البِحارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 6], with doubling, and it is also read «سُجِرَتْ» without doubling. As for the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ», it was said that it is in the sense of «فُجِّرَتْ» (burst forth). It was also said: «سُجِّرَتْ» means filled; and from it is «اَلْبَحْرُ المَسْجُورُ», the filled sea. And it was said: the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ» is: their waters were made into fires with which the people of the Fire are punished.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾: every faction was paired with those it followed. It was also said: they were paired with their deeds; and it was said: the bodies were paired with the souls.

zajjaj:8-9.t:
﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ — it is also read «وَإذا المَوْؤُودَةُ سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ» ("and when the girl buried alive asks for what sin she was killed"). «اَلْمَوْؤُودَةُ» is the one whom the Arabs used to bury alive: when a daughter was born to one of them, he buried her alive. The meaning of her being asked "For what sin was she killed?!" is to reproach (tabkīt) her killer on the Day of Resurrection, because her answer is: "I was killed without any sin." Like this reproach is Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ قالَ سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116]: the question to him and his answer are only a reproach to those who claimed this about him. One says «وَأدْتُ، أئِدُ، وأْدًا» when I bury the newborn alive; the agent is «وائِدٌ», the feminine agent «وائِدَةٌ», and the feminine plural «وائِداتٌ». Al-Farazdaq said:
؎وَمِنّا الَّذِي مَنَعَ الوائِدا ∗∗∗ تِ فَأحْيا الوَئِيدَ ولَمْ يُوأدِ
(And among us is he who stopped the women who buried girls alive, so he gave life to the one to be buried, and she was not buried.)
Likewise, for whoever read «سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ», her asking is a reproach to her killer.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَإذا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ﴾, and «نَشَرَتْ» (also read): the scrolls are spread open, and every person is given his book in his right hand or in his left, according to his deeds.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ — it was also read «قُشِطَتْ» with qāf — and the meaning of both is "stripped off", as a roof is stripped off. One says «كَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» and «قَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» with one meaning. Qāf and kāf are frequently substituted one for the other; like that is «لَبَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ» and «لَبَقْتُهُ» when I mix it.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾ and «سُعِرَتْ», with doubling and without; its meaning is "kindled", and likewise ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾, except that ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾ means "kindled time after time".

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾, that is: it was brought near to the God-fearing. The answer to these things is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أحْضَرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 14], that is: when these things which belong to the Day of Resurrection come about, at that time every soul will know what it has brought — that is, of deeds — and will be rewarded according to its deeds.

zajjaj:15-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ ﴿الجَوارِ الكُنَّسِ﴾: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ», and «اَلْجَوارِي» is the plural of «جارِيَةٌ», from «جَرى، يَجْرِي» (to run). «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ» and «خانِسَةٌ», and likewise «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is the plural of «كانِسٌ» and «كانِسَةٌ». The meaning is "So I swear", and «لا» is emphatic. As for «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here, most of the exegesis says the stars are meant by it, because they recede (takhnis), that is, disappear, because the meaning of ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 17] ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 18]…
«[Translator's note: the sentence beginning "because the meaning of…" breaks off in the source without completion.]»
The meaning of «اَلْخُنَّسُ» and «اَلْكُنَّسُ» with regard to the stars is that they rise running, and likewise recede, that is, disappear, and likewise they «تَكْنُسُ»: they enter their lair (kinās), that is, they disappear in the places where they disappear. It was also said: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here means the wild cows and the wild gazelles. «خُنَّسٌ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ»: gazelles are khunnas and cows are khunnas; «اَلْخَنْسُ» is shortness of the nose and its lying back from the mouth. If it refers to the cows or to the gazelles, then the meaning of «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is: those that «تَكْنُسُ», that is, enter the kinās, which is a branch of the branches of trees.

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾: one says «عَسْعَسَ اللَّيْلُ» when the night approaches, and «عَسْعَسَ» when it departs. The two meanings come back to one thing, namely the beginning of darkness at its start and its departure at its end.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾: when it extends until it becomes clear daylight. The answer to the oath in these things — I mean ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 15] and what follows it — is His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 19], meaning that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي العَرْشِ مَكِينٍ﴾: it was said that part of the strength of Jibrīl ﷺ is that he overturned the city of the people of Lūṭ with the front feathers of his wing, and they were four towns.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾: this too is an answer to the oath. The meaning is: "So I swear by these things that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace, and I swear by these things that your companion is not mad," meaning by it the Prophet ﷺ, because they said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6], so He said: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 1] ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Qalam: 2], and He said in this place: ﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾.
﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالأُفُقِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 23]: we have explained that in Sūrat al-Najm.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿وَما هو عَلى الغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾ — it is also read «بِظَنِينٍ». Whoever read «بِظَنِينٍ», its meaning is: he is not suspect regarding the unseen; he is trustworthy in what he conveyed from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. One says «ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا» in the sense of «اِتَّهَمْتُ زَيْدًا» ("I suspected Zayd"). Whoever read ﴿بِضَنِينٍ﴾, its meaning is: "he is not niggardly regarding the unseen", that is: he ﷺ conveys from Allah and teaches the Book of Allah.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَأيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "So what road will you take that is clearer than this way which I have made clear to you?!"

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿لِمَن شاءَ مِنكم أنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾, that is: uprightness is clear to you, so whoever wishes takes the road of truth and moderation, which is faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. Then He informed them that the will regarding granting success (tawfīq) belongs to Him, and that they are not able to do that except by the will of Allah and His granting of success, saying: ﴿وَما تَشاءُونَ إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 29]. A further proof of that is: ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ [Hūd: 88]. This is a notification that man does no good except by Allah's granting of success, and no evil except by Allah's forsaking him, because good and evil are by His decree and His measuring: He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إلَيْهِ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 13].
